correctness.rationale: For every nondegenerate complex r, all four conic determinants are nonzero. Five pairwise equation differences are squares/products defining 10 tacnodes, while Q+ and Q- have one tacnode and exactly two nodes. This uniquely marks the Q+/Q- pair. The three intrinsic marks (their tacnode, node secant, tangent) force a projectivity to [a x+b y:c y:d z]; the unordered distinct nodes force b=0 and a/c=+/-1; the Q+ mixed coefficient forces d/c=+/-1. All four possibilities preserve the union. Embedded exact ring checks replay the relevant polynomial identities and transformations.

value.rationale: Eleven tacnodes is the extremal natural contact configuration for four smooth conics, with a literature-classified parameter family. Its complete projective stabilizer and absence of exceptional parameters are structural moduli invariants, and the computation explains why the abstract component-contact graph overestimates geometric component permutations. This is a complete parameter-uniform classification, not an arbitrary numeric slice or a repackaging of known syzygies.
